## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The legacy fetcher's 8-attempt retry loop must be fixed before merge: it breaks the project's 3-attempt retry cap, and the only exemption is the one this pull request adds to the rules itself. The fetcher also does not retry a connection dropped mid-body, which is the failure the retries are meant to absorb.

## Changes
Adds `app/legacy/fetch.py` (inventory fetch with up to 8 attempts) and `app/health.py` (health probe with up to 3 attempts), with parametrized tests for both in `tests/test_retries.py`. Adds a sentence to `docs/review-rules.md` exempting modules under `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Keep the legacy fetcher within the 3-attempt retry cap — When the legacy service is down, `fetch_inventory` makes 8 attempts, which breaks "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." (`docs/review-rules.md:5`, applied through `AGENTS.md:3`). The only exemption is `docs/review-rules.md:7`, which this pull request adds, so it cannot authorize the code it ships with. — A down legacy service holds each calling worker thread for up to 87 seconds (8 timeouts of 10 s plus 7 delays of 1 s), the harm the rule names. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS` to 3, or land the exemption as a separate change approved by the rule's owners and bounded in attempts or total wait.

## Important
- app/legacy/fetch.py:24 — correctness — Retry a connection dropped mid-body in fetch_inventory — When the legacy service sends headers and then closes the connection before the full body, `resp.read()` raises `http.client.IncompleteRead`, which is not an `OSError`, so `except OSError` does not retry it. The pull-request description gives dropped connections during the nightly restart as the reason for the retries; `app/health.py:24` has the same handler. — A fetch that loses its connection mid-body during the nightly restart fails on the first attempt instead of being retried. — Fix: Catch `http.client.HTTPException` alongside `OSError` at this line and extend `test_returns_body` with a response whose `read()` raises `IncompleteRead`.
